repos.description: Computer use CLI for AI agents
repos.readme_text:
# agent-desktop Computer use for AI agents: read and operate desktop apps through the OS accessibility tree.

A CLI and C library for macOS, Windows and Linux. A snapshot returns JSON with a ref for every element an agent can act on. The agent acts on a ref and snapshots again to check, with no pixel matching; the loop stays in your agent. Every CLI call runs in its own process. Headless calls still prohibit foreground activation and synthesized input. Snapshots, clipboard reads, screenshots, command output and debug artifacts can contain private desktop content. Keep them out of public logs and uploads. The optional [JEV helper](skills/jev-desktop/SKILL.md) sends screen descriptions to a configured model provider; it is separate from the native CLI. See [privacy and data handling](docs/faq.md#what-data-can-contain-private-information). ## Installation Install on macOS, Windows or Linux with npm: ```bash npm install -g agent-desktop agent-desktop version ``` Bun, Yarn and pnpm can install the same package. It includes native binaries and platform helpers for x64 and ARM64. For direct execution without a JavaScript launcher, download the matching native archive from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/releases) and keep its helper beside the executable. Official Homebrew and Scoop packages are being submitted; they are not yet available in the default catalogs. The repository no longer maintains a custom Homebrew tap or Scoop bucket. - **macOS** needs Accessibility permission: `agent-desktop permissions --guide`. - **Windows** needs no grant for apps at your terminal's integrity level. - **Linux** needs the user's graphical session with `at-spi2-core`. See [installation and permissions](docs/install.md) for package-manager behavior, release archives, and building from source. ## Quick start Observe, act on a ref, observe again. Any app name from `agent-desktop list-apps` works; Finder is the macOS example. Each command prints one JSON envelope; a trimmed snapshot follows the commands. ```bash agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-desktop click @s8f3k2p9:e8 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # observe again to verify ``` ```json { "version": "2.6", "ok": true, "command": "snapshot", "data": { "app": "Finder", "window": { "id": "w-204749", "title": "Downloads" }, "snapshot_id": "s8f3k2p9", "ref_count": 59, "complete": true, "tree": { "role": "window", "name": "Downloads", "children": [ { "role": "treeitem", "name": "Documents", "ref_id": "@s8f3k2p9:e8", "available_actions": ["Click"] } ] } } } ``` - **Refs belong to their snapshot.** A bare `@e8` is rejected with `INVALID_ARGS`. When the UI changes, an action returns `STALE_REF` or `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`: take a new snapshot and use its refs. - **Several windows** give `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`; `snapshot` lists the candidate window ids in `error.details`. repos.readme_text:
# nanochat

![nanochat logo](dev/nanochat.png)
![scaling laws](dev/scaling_laws_jan26.png)

nanochat is the simplest experimental harness for training LLMs. It is designed to run on a single GPU node, the code is minimal/hackable, and it covers all major LLM stages including tokenization, pretraining, finetuning, evaluation, and inference. For example, you can train your own GPT-2 capability LLM (which cost ~$43,000 to train in 2019) for only $48 (~2 hours of 8XH100 GPU node) and then talk to it over a simple CLI. On a spot instance, the total cost can be closer to ~$15. More generally, nanochat is configured out of the box to train an entire miniseries of compute-optimal models by setting one single complexity dial: `--depth`, the number of layers in the GPT transformer model (GPT-2 capability happens to be approximately depth 26). All other hyperparameters (the width of the transformer, number of heads, learning rate adjustments, training horizons, weight decays, ...) are calculated automatically in an optimal way.

For questions about the repo, I recommend either using [DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/karpathy/nanochat) from Devin/Cognition to ask questions about the repo, or use the [Discussions tab](https://github.com/karpathy/nanochat/discussions), or come by the [#nanochat](https://discord.com/channels/1020383067459821711/1427295580895314031) channel on Discord.

## Time-to-GPT-2 Leaderboard

Presently, the main focus of development is on tuning the pretraining stage, which takes the most amount of compute. Inspired by the modded-nanogpt repo and to incentivise progress and community collaboration, nanochat maintains a leaderboard for a "GPT-2 speedrun", which is the wall-clock time required to train a nanochat model to GPT-2 grade capability, as measured by the DCLM CORE score. The [runs/speedrun.sh](runs/speedrun.sh) script always reflects the reference way to train GPT-2 grade model and talk to it. The current leaderboard looks as follows:

| # | time | val_bpb | CORE | Description | Date | Commit | Contributors |
|---|-------------|---------|------|-------------|------|--------|--------------|
| 0 | 168 hours | - | 0.2565 | Original OpenAI GPT-2 checkpoint | 2019 | - | OpenAI |
| 1 | 3.04 | 0.74833 | 0.2585 | d24 baseline, slightly overtrained | Jan 29 2026 | 348fbb3 | @karpathy |
| 2 | 2.91 | 0.74504 | 0.2578 | d26 slightly undertrained **+fp8** | Feb 2 2026 | a67eba3 | @karpathy |
| 3 | 2.76 | 0.74645 | 0.2602 | bump total batch size to 1M tokens | Feb 5 2026 | 2c062aa | @karpathy |
| 4 | 2.02 | 0.71854 | 0.2571 | change dataset to NVIDIA ClimbMix | Mar 4 2026 | 324e69c | @ddudek @karpathy |
| 5 | 1.80 | 0.71808 | 0.2690 | autoresearch [round 1](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2031135152349524125) | Mar 9 2026 | 6ed7d1d | @karpathy |
| 6 | 1.65 | 0.71800 | 0.2626 | autoresearch round 2 | Mar 14 2026 | a825e63 | @karpathy |

The primary metric we care about is "time to GPT-2" - the wall clock time needed to outperform the GPT-2 (1.6B) CORE metric on an 8XH100 GPU node. The GPT-2 CORE score is 0.256525. In 2019, the training of GPT-2 cost approximately $43,000 so it is incredible that due to many advances over 7 years across the stack, we can now do so much faster and for well below $100 (e.g. at the current ~$3/GPU/hr, an 8XH100 node is ~$24/hr, so 2 hours is ~$48).

See [dev/LEADERBOARD.md](dev/LEADERBOARD.md) for more docs on how to interpret and contribute to the leaderboard.

## Getting started

### Setup

nanochat uses [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for dependency management. To install:

```bash
uv sync --extra gpu    # Use for CUDA (A100/H100/etc.)
uv sync --extra cpu    # (or) Use for CPU-only / MPS
source .venv/bin/activate
```

For development (adds pytest, matplotlib, ipykernel, transformers, etc.):

```bash
uv sync --extra gpu --group dev
```

### Reproduce and talk to GPT-2

The most fun you can have is to train your own GPT-2 and talk to it. The entire pipeline to do so is contained in the single file

repos.readme_text:
# Heretic ### Training-free language model modification **Remove censorship**, suppress slop, reduce sycophancy, and more.
All in an afternoon, on your gaming PC. [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1447831134212984903?color=5865F2&label=discord&labelColor=black&logo=discord&logoColor=white&style=for-the-badge)](https://discord.gg/gdXc48gSyT)     [![Matrix](https://img.shields.io/badge/Matrix-black?logo=matrix&style=for-the-badge)](https://matrix.to/#/#heretic:matrix.org)    [![Follow us on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/badges/resolve/main/follow-us-on-hf-md-dark.svg)](https://huggingface.co/heretic-org)    [![Codeberg mirror](https://img.shields.io/badge/Codeberg%20mirror-black?logo=codeberg&style=for-the-badge)](https://codeberg.org/p-e-w/heretic)
-----   [![#1 Repository of the Day](https://trendshift.io/api/badge/repositories/20538)](https://trendshift.io/repositories/20538)     [![Model and download statistics](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9b5a660-7ef9-43c7-991c-fd9d63ea8bd8)](https://heretic.sdad.pro/) ## Modify any LLM that you can run on your hardware[^1] [^1]: Heretic supports on-the-fly 4-bit model quantization with bitsandbytes, which can reduce the amount of VRAM required to process a model to the same amount that is used to run a typical quantized version of it, at a slight accuracy cost. Set the `quantization` option to `bnb_4bit` to enable this. Heretic is a unique tool that lets you do what only corporations with access to massive computing power usually do: *Modify,* rather than merely run, language models. It does not perform expensive training; rather, it uses a collection of mathematical techniques to steer behavior based on contrasting example prompts and matching scorers. Heretic can, depending on the configuration: * **Suppress refusals/remove censorship** (this is the [default action](/config.default.toml)) * Reduce slop ([`config.noslop.toml`](/config.noslop.toml)) * Reduce humor ([`config.nohumor.toml`](/config.nohumor.toml)) * Reduce sycophancy ([`config.nosyco.toml`](/config.nosyco.toml)) * Alter emotional alignment ([`config.emotions.toml`](/config.emotions.toml)) and many, many other things. ### :bangbang: Using Heretic does NOT require understanding how language models work internally :bangbang: In fact, you can go from zero to removing censorship from your first model [in a matter of seconds](#usage). Heretic supports most dense models, including many multimodal models, several different MoE architectures, and many modern hybrid models. The community has created and published [thousands](https://huggingface.co/models?other=heretic) of models with Heretic. Heretic models have been independently benchmarked using standard metrics like MMLU and GSM8K, and have been found to compare favorably against models produced with competing abliteration tools.[^2][^3] [^2]: https://old.reddit.com/r/LocalLLaMA/comments/1sojjoc/abliterlitics_benchmark_and_tensor_analysis/ [^3]: https://old.reddit.com/r/LocalLLaMA/comments/1sy18lx/abliterlitics_benchmarks_and_tensor_comparison/     ## Usage Prepare a Python 3.10+ environment with PyTorch 2.6+ installed as appropriate for your hardware. Then run: ```sh pip install -U heretic-llm heretic Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 ``` Replace `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507` with whatever model you want to process. **By default, Heretic performs censorship removal (refusal suppression).** If you want to do something else, choose one of the configuration files linked above, or write your own. See [`config.default.toml`](/config.default.toml)
